en: Modern papers combine GNSS point velocities with InSAR maps so both the exact station motion and the spatial pattern of displacement are measured.
Published plate velocities include uncertainty; a modern process reports both the displacement rate and how large the measurement error is.
The competency asks you to name processes such as GNSS, InSAR, VLBI, or seafloor acoustics, not only to say that plates move slowly.
Investigate with carts and marbles, not by crashing bikes or bodies; the competency is about models of collisions, not dangerous tests.
A light paper ball at the far end of a stretched slinky moves when the wave arrives, showing the wave carried energy to it.
Placing three paper markers along a slinky shows that wave energy weakens with distance, because the farthest marker moves the least.
Intensity is measured by collecting reports from many places about how people felt the shaking and what damage they saw.
A seismograph draws its wiggly lines on paper or a screen, and that record is called a seismogram.
News reports usually name an earthquake by its epicenter, such as a quake near a town, even though the focus is underground.
A motor gets its energy from a battery or a wall outlet, while a generator gets its energy from a crank, a turbine, or an engine, so their energy sources are opposite.
An animal's label in a food chain is based on its usual diet, so a pig that eats both plants and scraps is an omnivore even if it sometimes eats only plants.
The Sun is not a living thing, so it is never labeled as a herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore; it is only the source of energy.
A leaf partially covered with black paper tests light needs, because the covered and uncovered halves share the same leaf.
A struck tuning fork held near a light paper ball makes the ball sway, showing that sound waves carry energy through the air.
To correct the idea that sound pushes air forward, observe that a light paper strip near a speaker vibrates but does not fly away.
Label every component in a circuit diagram with its symbol and value, such as ohms for a resistor, so another person can read it.
Draw a circuit diagram with the battery on one side and arrange wires so they do not cross, because crossing lines confuse the reader.
A dominant allele is a gene version that shows its trait even when a different version is paired with it, so only one copy is needed to see the trait.
A recessive allele only shows its trait when a person has two copies of it, so one copy stays hidden if the other allele is dominant.
Hold the test tube against a dark background, like black paper, so the white precipitate is easier to see clearly.
Check the limewater against a white paper before starting to make sure it is clear and has not already turned cloudy.
When drawing a circuit diagram, include a legend that explains each symbol, so a reader who does not know the symbols can still follow.
A circuit diagram should show the switch in the open or closed position used in the experiment, so the reader knows the state.
Comparing how much energy each wave type carries uses the same spring and push strength, and measures how far a paper cup at the far end slides.
Label each test tube with the sample name before testing so the results from different gases or liquids are not mixed up.
The investigator draws the leaf outline on white paper with a pencil before adding iodine, because pencil marks do not wash away in the liquids.
A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius, the same unit used for weather reports in the Philippines.
The unit gram is about the mass of one small paper clip, so a kilogram is one thousand grams.
Each PAGASA bulletin gives the typhoon's latest coordinates and wind speed, which are used to update the plotted track.
Label the x-axis with what you changed and the y-axis with what you measured, so the graph is clear.
